articles.title: 'I lost my hero': the heartbreaking message from Gary Myers' son after his death'
articles.standfirst: The historic NASCAR driver and patriarch of a family connected to motorsports for four generations died at the age of 76. His sons Burt and Jason bid him farewell with heartfelt messages.
articles.summary: The historic NASCAR driver and patriarch of a family connected to motorsports for four generations died at the age of 76. His sons Burt and Jason bid him farewell with heartfelt messages.
articles.body:
G ary Myers died on Thursday, September 10 in North Carolina , the state that was home throughout his entire motor racing career. With his passing, American motorsports bids farewell to one of the figures who helped build a family tradition that spanned four generations.

The news was formally confirmed by his sons, Burt and Jason Myers , who shared emotional farewell messages on their social media to honor the memory of their father and mentor.

Who was Gary Myers, the patriarch of a NASCAR family?

Motorsports fans know and deeply respect Gary Myers for embodying the purest, closest, and most passionate spirit of grassroots racing in the United States.

' Myers belonged to one of the most storied families in NASCAR . Four generations of his family have raced on the asphalt of the legendary Bowman Gray Stadium in Winston-Salem, North Carolina, nicknamed "The Madhouse" because of the extremely high tension of its short-track oval races.'

Gary spent more than 60 years of his life glued to the racetracks. Fans watched him grow up from being a child watching his father race, then competing fiercely as a driver and, finally, staying in the pits guiding the steps of his own sons and grandson. Having competed side by side against his sons on the same track created an immense and deeply endearing emotional connection with the local public.

Although he competed in 46 races in NASCAR’s top category ( NASCAR Winston Cup Series) during the 1970s, Myers always did so as an independent driver . This means he built and maintained his own vehicles on very tight budgets, competing directly against the millionaire teams of the era.

One of his greatest achievements came in 1996, when he won the SMART Modified Tour championship. The organization itself remembered him as one of its founding members and highlighted the 15 victories he achieved in the category.

The message that moved the NASCAR family

Burt Myers's farewell revealed the most personal dimension of the loss. The driver was one of the first members of the family to speak out publicly and remembered Gary as his great “hero,” a figure whose importance extended far beyond the world of racing.

“Last night I lost my hero” , Burt wrote. The message reflected the personal dimension of a loss that transcends results and trophies.

"Last night I lost my hero. He fought with all his strength, but he was very tired. I’m sure he is now in heaven doing the things he couldn’t do in recent years." His message reflected both his personal pain and the deep relationship they had.

Jason Myers joined in the outpouring of affection and described Gary as the family's “patriarch”. He also recalled his close relationship with his children and his influence on the generations that kept the family tradition alive on the racetracks.

The story of Gary Myers does not end with his death. His father Billy and his uncle Bobby were part of the family's first generations on the tracks; then came Burt and Jason, and finally Slate, who began his career in 2024.

So far, the family has not publicly reported the cause of death. What remains confirmed is the legacy of a man who spent decades in motorsports and who ended up becoming the center of one of the families most closely connected to Bowman Gray .

articles.title: NASCAR fight night: Blaney and Hocevar exchange punches after late-race contact at Bristol
articles.standfirst: It was an explosive post-race encounter full of emotions and intensity
articles.summary: It was an explosive post-race encounter full of emotions and intensity
articles.body:
Joey Logano pulled off one of the most impressive late-race charges of the NASCAR season Saturday night at Bristol Motor Speedway . Yet within minutes of taking the checkered flag in the Bass Pro Shops Night Race, his victory had become a secondary storyline.

Instead, the spotlight shifted to a fiery confrontation between Ryan Blaney and Carson Hocevar that escalated into one of the most dramatic post-race altercations NASCAR has seen in recent years. The tension stemmed from a controversial late-race incident involving the two drivers.

As the race wound down at Bristol, contact between Hocevar and Blaney ended with Blaney's car crashing, instantly igniting frustration from the former Cup Series champion and setting the stage for an explosive post-race encounter. Anyone expecting a calm conversation on pit road was quickly disappointed.

As soon as the race ended and drivers exited their cars, anticipation spread throughout the garage and grandstands. Fans understood that emotions were running high and that Blaney was unlikely to let the incident pass without confrontation. They were right.

Near Hocevar's No. 77 Spire Motorsports Chevrolet, Blaney stormed toward the young driver and immediately shoved him. Hocevar responded with a punch to Blaney's face , turning the confrontation into a full-blown fight.

What followed was a chaotic scene

Officials, crew members, and team personnel rushed into the middle of the altercation as Blaney repeatedly tried to push through those attempting to separate the two drivers. Witnesses described a furious Blaney, who continued pointing toward Hocevar and shouting as team members escorted him away from the scene.

It was a level of anger rarely seen from the Team Penske driver. Blaney has been involved in heated moments throughout his NASCAR career , but this appeared to rank among the most emotional post-race reactions of his time in the Cup Series. The crowd loved every second of it.

Thousands of fans seated in Bristol's backstretch grandstands had a clear view of the confrontation. As the altercation unfolded, spectators stood, cheered, and reacted to every shove and punch. The response only intensified afte r Blaney was finally pulled away from the scene.

Hocevar, meanwhile, remained near his car and appeared to acknowledge the crowd's reaction, drawing even more noise from fans who had just witnessed one of the night's most memorable moments. Fortunately, neither driver appeared to suffer any injuries during the incident.

Another controversial chapter to Hocevar's reputation

Even after the confrontation ended, the drama lingered. Hocevar stayed between his race car and the pit wall for several minutes, talking with team members and delaying any immediate comments to reporters about either the crash or the fight.

The incident added another controversial chapter to Hocevar's growing reputation as one of NASCAR's most aggressive young drivers. The 23-year-old has built a reputation for racing hard and refusing to back down, traits that have earned him both admirers and critics throughout the garage. Saturday night's clash with Blaney is unlikely to change those opinions.

Bristol's half-mile concrete ova l has long been known for producing intense emotions. The track's tight confines, heavy traffic, and constant physical racing often create rivalries and grudges that extend beyond the checkered flag. Saturday's race delivered another example of why Bristol remains one of NASCAR's most unpredictable venues.
